did.physloc: Stanford Archive of Recorded Sound Stanford University Libraries Stanford, California 94305-3076
did.abstract: Open reel tape recordings of the "Annals of Jazz" radio program produced and hosted by historian and educator Richard Hadlock, broadcast on KCSM, San Mateo between 1982 and 1991. The interviews in the collection feature many Jazz luminaries at the peak of their careers and have on occasion been broadcast on KCSM. Lastly, Richard Hadlock was also an active musical performer on reed instruments, many of the live music recordings in this collection feature him.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: the Richard Hadlock Jazz Radio, Live Music, and Artist Interview Collection, ARS-0065. Courtesy of the Stanford Archive of Recorded Sound, Stanford University Libraries, Stanford, Calif.

acqinfo.head: Source
acqinfo.p: The Richard Hadlock Annals of Jazz Collection was donated to the Stanford Archive of Recorded Sound by Richard Hadlock in October 2006. The artist interviews and live performance recordings were donated in July 2021.

did.unittitle: Annals of Jazz radio show program recordings

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Richard Hadlock Annals of Jazz Collection consists of selected tapes from jazz historian and educator Richard Hadlock's venerable radio series Annals of Jazz, as broadcast on radio station KCSM in San Mateo, California from 1982-1991. Hadlock, a musician, publisher (Record Changer magazine) and author (Downbeat, Metronome and the book Jazz Masters of the Twenties), began Annals of Jazz on KJAZ in 1959, followed by eighteen years at KQED, and has been at KCSM for over twenty years. The tapes in this collection appear to have originated at KQED but were labeled and numbered by KCSM with new air dates. The programs examine musicians, composers, performance styles, movements, and instrumentation, largely from the classic era before free jazz, jazz rock and fusion became prevalent. Outside of Hadlock's commentary, the series contains little unpublished content, although there is an interview with clarinetist Bob Helm from 1984 (which aired on KCSM 5/6/89).

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Some of the musicians profiled: Duke Ellington, Red Norvo, Bunny Berigan, Jelly Roll Morton, Lennie Tristano, Coleman Hawkins, Fats Waller, John Lewis, Johnny Hodges, Benny Goodman, Roy Eldridge, Lester Young, Bob Brookmeyer, Miles Davis, Adrian Rollini, Isham Jones, Charles Mingus, Don Redman, the Dodds Brothers, the Jones Brothers, James P. Johnson, Jack Teagarden, Art Pepper, Sidney Bechet, Earl Hines, Teddy Wilson, Bud Freeman, Thelonious Monk, Barney Bigard, Count Basie, Red Nichols, John Coltrane, Eddie Sauter, Lee Konitz, Lionel Hampton, Joe Thomas, George Mitchell, Turk Murphy, Harry James, Django Reinhardt, Bobby Hackett, Lawrence Brown, Clarence Williams, Ben Webster, Irving Fazola, Gerry Mullifan, Ruby Braff, Dizzy Gillespie, Stan Getz, Mary Lou Williams, Wingy Manone, King Oliver, Woody Herman, Tony Scott, Billy Butterfield, Art Hodes, Bennie Moten, Artie Shaw, and Fats Navarro.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Some of the songwriters profiled: Vincent Youmans, Richard Whiting, Walter Donaldson, Victor Young, Nacio Herb Brown, Ray Henderson, Jerome Kern, Harold Arlen, Fred Ahlert, and Arthur Schwartz.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Some of the subjects covered: Bay Area Jazz, Jazz as Sacred Music, The Joy of Hokum, Forgotten Tenors, Western Swing, and Territory Bands.

odd.head: General
odd.p: Whenever possible the perfomers are listed in a scope and content note. The listings reflect the names and instruments as marked on the recordings. If Richard Hadlock is not listed as a performer on the carrier, the cassette is in the perofrmances by various artists sub-series. There is a possibility Richard Hadlock is a performer but is not listed on the carrier the recording is under "Performances by Various Artists" and has an added note. Please be aware this does not mean Richard Hadlock is not performing on a recording in the "Performances by Various Artists" sub-series, it is intended to be interpreted as there is nothing suggesting he is.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This drive contains digital transfers and spreadsheet of information about the physical media in the two series "Musical Performances" and "Interviews." These were completed independently by Duane Gordon before the recordings were donated to the Archive of Recorded Sound.
